explanation: Work done by a constant force is W = F*d*cos(theta), the product of the displacement with the COMPONENT of force along that displacement. Only F*cos(theta) does work, so a force perpendicular to the motion (theta = 90 degrees, cos = 0) does zero work, and a force with a backward component (theta > 90 degrees) does NEGATIVE work. Work is a scalar measured in joules, and on the AP exam it is the dot product F·d. The animation slides a block through a fixed displacement while you set the force magnitude and its angle, showing the F*cos(theta) component and the live W readout.
bullets: Only the force component along d, F*cos(theta), does work.
theta = 90 degrees gives cos = 0, so perpendicular forces do zero work.
theta > 90 degrees makes cos negative, so the work is negative.
Work is a scalar (the dot product F·d), in joules.
